title: Hourly usage proration reconciler for interval-aligned billing and rate-limit credits
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: mid-cycle hourly usage buckets and transient rate-limit throttles are producing incorrect proration lines in the Stripe/NetSuite export. We observe two related error classes: 1) negative proration artifacts when burst credits or quota refunds are applied mid-billing-hour, and 2) duplicate adjustment lines when the export job retries on transient failures without idempotent keys. Both lead to invoice mismatches and manual CFO reconciliation work. This ticket implements a reconciler that operates on hourly deltas, generates idempotent synthetic adjustment lines for NetSuite, and emits deterministic Stripe credit/refund operations when required. The reconciler must handle: (a) requests throttled by per-customer rate limits; (b) automatic quota refunds triggered by provisioning changes; (c) cross-hour requests that span billing boundaries; and (d) export job retries without double-counting.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler computes hourly usage deltas for all customers and produces a single adjustment per hour with idempotency key
No negative-proration lines appear in NetSuite exports caused by rate-limit refund races for >99% of test customers
Retrying export job using same idempotency token results in no duplicate invoice lines in NetSuite and no duplicate Stripe credit events
End-to-end integration test that simulates a burst (500 requests/min), partial quota refund, and an export retry shows invoice parity between Stripe charges and NetSuite lines
New metric: billing.reconciler.adjustments_created (labels: customer_id, reason) is emitted and visible on billing dashboard
implementation_notes: Compute canonical hourly buckets using UTC-aligned hour boundaries and assign each request to bucket based on request_end_time (not start_time) to avoid split-request ambiguity
Introduce 'proration_intent' field on usage rows that describes source: chargeback|quota_refund|rate_limit_credit
Generate idempotency key: reconv1:{customer_id}:{hour_start_iso}:{reason_checksum} and persist in reconciliation table with exact hash of adjustment payload
For Stripe credits, use a single top-level refund/credit operation per hour per customer; attach metadata referencing NetSuite export line_id to cross-link systems
NetSuite export: create Adjustment line with externalId = idempotency_key and export_job_version header to detect mismatched schema
Add safety guard: if reconciler detects >3 conflicting deltas for same hour, mark customer for manual review and create incident ticket with priority escalation
Implement fuzzy-match dedupe in export consumer: if an incoming adjustment externalId already exists in NetSuite, skip and emit billing.reconciler.duplicate_skipped metric
work_log_and_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed to confirm best bucket key. Found existing usage rows sometimes use request_start_time causing split attribution; proposed switch to request_end_time. Spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/BR-42789-spike
2026-02-25: Design review with PM and Finance. PM recommended single-credit-per-hour to minimize NSF and downstream matching. Finance flagged need for NetSuite externalId for every adjustment.

2026-03-01: Prototype reconciler implemented in billing-service branch feat/eng-42789. Uses materialized view hourly_usage_hour_delta_v1. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1837

2026-03-04: Integration test failing: duplicate externalId created when job restarted; root cause was missing transactional upsert around idempotency table. Added DB transactional lock sketch to PR comments.
2026-03-07: Fixed race by using SELECT FOR UPDATE on reconciliation_keys table. End-to-end local test passes for retry scenarios. Pushed patch to branch.

2026-03-09: Load test with 10k simulated customers running burst patterns completed. Observed 0.4% flagged-for-manual-review rate; next step is tune dedupe fuzz threshold and improve logging for those customers.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: transient DB locks could slow reconciliation job causing export latency. Mitigation: process customers in smaller shards and add backoff/retry with exponential jitter
Risk: NetSuite schema changes may reject externalId. Mitigation: export_job_version header and small-canary export for first 100 customers
Risk: incorrect mapping between Stripe credits and NetSuite adjustment IDs. Mitigation: attach cross-reference metadata and run nightly parity job that compares Stripe ledger with NetSuite lines
next_steps: Finish PR review and merge feat/eng-42789
Canary reconciler on 10% of customers for one billing cycle and monitor billing.reconciler.adjustments_created and billing.reconciler.manual_review_rate
Coordinate with Finance to schedule NetSuite schema validation and small-canary export run
After canary, expand to 100% and add nightly parity alert if mismatch > 0.1%
